scope: Audit all 28 direct skill-event mappings for event classification, evidence-source presence, and confidence semantics.
findings: All 28 mappings resolve to an existing registered event and have non-empty source_ids.
Chapter 1 and Beast have direct official skill/content evidence.
Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 remain appropriately marked corroborated because the available official material establishes event scope while the individual names come from maintained independent catalogs.

Chapter 4 retains three direct reward/content mappings and one corroborated aggregate named-move mapping; the official release evidence establishes the event but does not by itself name every individual move in accessible text.

The six DAIMA Pack skills remain direct_scope rather than direct-name mappings because the official release source establishes the pack's six skills but the accessible announcement does not provide a six-name text mapping. The existing canonical records supply the individual identities.
No mapping justifies assigning a game version or patch number from its release/event date.
policy: Research and verification timestamps are not game versions.
Do not upgrade evidence confidence merely because a skill's DLC requirement matches an event.
Preserve unresolved historical identity gaps rather than inferring internal IDs.
next: Continue with mechanics enrichment for the Chapter 4 quartet and separately audit Free Update 20 Festival recovery evidence; do not reopen already reconciled event mappings unless new primary evidence appears.
